newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian navy rescues crew from sinking ship.
newsitem.headline: Indian navy rescues crew from sinking ship.

text.p: All 19 crew members of a ship sinking off Bombay harbour were rescued by naval helicopters on Friday, a defence ministry statement said.
It said the Indian Navy flew in its helicopters and rescued the crew soon after it received a dawn distress call from the captain of the cargo ship M.V. Sea Empress.

"Initially there was some fault in the engine room which could not be rectified and later there was uncontrollable flooding in the engine room and cargo hold," the statement quoted the ship's captain Jawed Ahmed Mufti as saying.
Mufti and the ship's chief engineer Dilawar Mohammad Gaus are Pakistanis while the rest of the crew is Indian.
The ship, owned by Dubai-based Bayat International Group and registered at Kingston Port, was carrying 4,200 tonnes of sulphur from Bahrain to Bombay, the statement said.
More than 30 people died in a similar incident in May this year when a cargo ship carrying sulphur overturned and sank off Bombay harbour.
